summary: Order submit failures (~31%) began at ~11:00-11:02 and persist through the latest data (12:58), caused by the external exchange provider (api.exchange-partner.example) degrading. exchange-gateway logs show upstream connect timeouts (5000ms) and 503 Service Unavailable from the partner beginning 11:01:25, and exchange-gateway upstream_latency jumped from ~120ms to ~9200ms while its own CPU/memory/request-rate stayed flat. order-service errors are purely propagated ("exchange-gateway call failed: 504 Gateway Timeout"). The order-service v2.15.2 deploy (10:48) was rolled back at 11:16 with NO recovery, and order-service failures started after exchange-gateway's — so the deploy is not the cause. This matches historical dependency_failure incident HIST-103. Root cause originates at the external exchange partner.

ranked_hypotheses.title: External exchange partner API degradation
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The third-party exchange provider (api.exchange-partner.example) started timing out/returning 503 at ~11:01. exchange-gateway's calls to it hang ~5s and fail ~46%, so placeOrder requests fail as 504s at order-service. exchange-gateway itself is healthy, so the fault originates at the external dependency.

causal_chain.claim: External exchange provider starts timing out / returning 503 (~11:01)
exchange-gateway upstream latency jumps 120ms -> ~9200ms and upstream error rate -> ~46%
order-service placeOrder calls to exchange-gateway exceed timeout and return 504
order-service error rate -> ~31%; api-gateway and market-data-service also degrade

assumptions: Logs mentioning host=api.exchange-partner.example and 'exchange-api returned 503' reflect genuine partner-side failures, not a local network/DNS fault misattributed to the partner
exchange-api has no telemetry (has_telemetry=false), so partner-side evidence is only visible indirectly via exchange-gateway

ranked_hypotheses.title: resource_exhaustion in exchange-gateway
ranked_hypotheses.statement: exchange-gateway's own resources (CPU/memory/connections) were exhausted, causing timeouts.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: exchange-gateway CPU (~30%), memory (~44%) and request rate (~272 req/s) were flat across the incident; failures are explicitly upstream to api.exchange-partner.example.

ranked_hypotheses.title: order-service v2.15.2 release introduced the fault
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The idempotency-key change in order-service v2.15.2 caused submit failures.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Errors began at exchange-gateway (11:01:25) before order-service's first error (11:02:45); order-service errors are purely propagated exchange-gateway 504s; and although v2.15.2 was rolled back at 11:16, failures continued unchanged through 12:58 with no recovery. A deploy-caused fault would have stopped at rollback.

ranked_hypotheses.title: config_change: pricing-engine cache TTL
ranked_hypotheses.statement: Shorter pricing quote cache TTL (cfg-2290) caused failures.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: The change was at 09:20, ~100 min before onset; pricing-engine logged zero errors/warnings; order-service errors are tied to the exchange path, not pricing; and the ordering of timings does not fit.

facts.statement: order-service's only error pattern is propagated exchange-gateway 504 Gateway Timeout on placeOrder, starting 11:02:45.
order-service error rate jumped to ~31% at 11:00 and stayed elevated through 12:50.
exchange-gateway upstream failures (connect timeout to api.exchange-partner.example and 503 from exchange-api) began at 11:01:25, before order-service errors.
exchange-gateway upstream latency rose from ~120ms to ~9200ms at 11:00 and stayed there.
exchange-gateway upstream error rate rose from ~0.3% to ~46%.
exchange-gateway's own CPU (~30%) and request rate (~272 req/s) were flat throughout, ruling out local overload.
order-service v2.15.2 (dep-5333) was deployed at 10:48 and rolled back at 11:16.
Failures continued unchanged for ~1h40m after the rollback (through 12:58), so the rollback did not restore service.
The impact spans multiple exchange-gateway consumers: api-gateway error_rate ~6% and market-data-service stale-quote warnings.
The only other change (pricing-engine cfg-2290, cache TTL 5->4s at 09:20) had no correlating errors (pricing-engine logged zero WARN/ERROR).
A prior incident (HIST-103) with identical symptoms was attributed to an external exchange partner outage (dependency_failure).

assumptions: exchange-api (external) has no direct telemetry (has_telemetry=false), so partner-side health is inferred solely from exchange-gateway logs/metrics
The 'api.exchange-partner.example' host and 'exchange-api returned 503' messages genuinely indicate a partner-side failure rather than a local network/DNS/certificate fault on our side
No other unrecorded change occurred on the external network path

timeline.event: order-service, exchange-gateway, api-gateway error rates and exchange-gateway upstream latency spike
First exchange-gateway upstream connect timeout to api.exchange-partner.example
market-data-service warns of stale quotes via exchange-gateway
exchange-gateway circuit breaker OPEN for exchange-api
order-service v2.15.2 rolled back — no recovery

recommended_actions.action: Engage the exchange provider / vendor and confirm the api.exchange-partner.example outage; request status and ETA
recommended_actions.rationale: Failures are entirely on the partner-side path; only the partner can fix the root cause.

recommended_actions.action: Fail over to a secondary exchange route / enable circuit-breaker fallback to route around the degraded partner (as in HIST-103)
recommended_actions.rationale: Removes customer-facing impact while the partner recovers.

recommended_actions.action: Do NOT roll back or chase the order-service deploy as the cause; keep v2.15.2 or re-deploy if desired since rollback showed no benefit
recommended_actions.rationale: Rollback at 11:16 produced no recovery; the deploy is not the fault.

recommended_actions.action: Add telemetry/alerting on exchange-gateway upstream_error_rate and upstream_latency_ms to detect partner degradation sooner
recommended_actions.rationale: exchange-api has no telemetry; the partner outage was only visible indirectly.

recommended_actions.action: Tune timeouts/retries and add graceful degradation for order submit when the exchange partner is down (queue or reject fast with clear messaging)
recommended_actions.rationale: Reduces blast radius of future partner outages across order-service, api-gateway and market-data-service.

data_gaps: No direct telemetry or logs from the external exchange provider (exchange-api) — partner-side root cause is inferred, not observed.
No network/DNS-level data for the host api.exchange-partner.example (e.g. TLS handshake failures or DNS resolution) to fully exclude a local connectivity fault masquerading as a partner outage.
No deployment history found for exchange-gateway (count=0), so we cannot fully exclude an unrecorded gateway-side configuration/network change on our side.

findings.statement: order-service first error appears at 11:02:45 and the only error pattern is 'exchange-gateway call failed: 504 Gateway Timeout (placeOrder)' (349 matches).

findings.statement: order-service error_rate was ~0.2% until 10:50, then jumped to 24.64% at 11:00 and stayed ~31% through 12:50.

exchange-gateway errors begin at 11:01:25 (earlier than order-service) and are upstream failures: 'upstream connect timeout after 5000ms host=api.exchange-partner.example op=placeOrder' and 'exchange-api returned 503 Service Unavailable'.

refs.quote: upstream connect timeout after 5000ms host=api.exchange-partner.example op=placeOrder

findings.statement: exchange-gateway upstream_latency_ms jumped from ~120ms to ~8248ms at 11:00 and remained ~9200ms through 12:50.
exchange-gateway upstream_error_rate rose from ~0.3% to ~46% at 11:00 and stayed elevated.
exchange-gateway's own resources were flat/healthy: cpu_pct ~30% and request_rate ~272 req/s unchanged across the incident window.
order-service deployment dep-5333 (v2.15.2, 'Add idempotency keys to order submit') went out 10:48 and was rolled back at 11:16.
After the 11:16 rollback, exchange-gateway errors continued unchanged through 12:58 (412 ERROR matches), and order-service error_rate stayed ~31% — no recovery.

api-gateway error_rate rose from ~0.2% to ~6% at 11:00 and stayed elevated, and market-data-service logged 'stale quotes: exchange feed lag ... via exchange-gateway' from 11:02:59 — showing the impact spans multiple exchange-gateway consumers.

refs.quote: stale quotes: exchange feed lag 4s via exchange-gateway

findings.statement: Only other change in window: pricing-engine config cfg-2290 cache.ttl_seconds 5->4 at 09:20; pricing-engine produced zero WARN/ERROR logs and no degrade.

Historical incident HIST-103 (2025-10-21) is the same pattern: order-service/exchange-gateway 504 on order submit, root cause 'External exchange API outage on the partner side', category dependency_failure.
